comments.author: PaulHoule
comments.story_title: Ask HN: Have You Consulted with Experts?
comments.why_zh: 专家解释了电能如何在导线之间流动，揭开了噪声和天线的神秘面纱。
comments.quote_zh: 一种鼓舞人心的洞见——电能并非在导线中流动，而是通过导线之间的空间流动
comments.text_zh: 某些类型的“专家”不过是大宗商品：你可以雇一个天文学博士或一名注册护士。创业者交易的则是一种特殊的专业知识：有价值、独特且可防御的知识产权。Ray Kroc 只需懂得如何教人们去教其他人经营麦当劳餐厅。一个实现了“产品-市场契合”的企业处于一种非常具体、路径依赖的境况。有时你发现了某种“一个奇怪的小窍门”，能让你在一段时间内大把赚钱，而这时你最想做的就是把它保密。另一些时候，知识过于特定（比如：你怎样才能在这个山谷里种出尽可能多的水稻？），对外人来说根本没什么兴趣。“专家网络”出了名地不设防，所以公司非常担心他们请来的专家带出去的有价值信息（例如“一个奇怪的小窍门”）会比带进来的更多。我最喜欢的那类专家是[视频]里的这种人：他在 40 多年的职业生涯中持续成长，从对电路板中的噪声一无所知，到形成一种鼓舞人心的洞见——电能并非在导线中流动，而是通过导线之间的空间流动，这让我原本觉得关于天线的一切神秘之处都变得显而易见。
comments.text: Some kinds of "expert" are a commodity: you can hire an astronomy PhD or a registered nurse. Entrepreneurs traffic in a special expertise: valuable, unique and defensible IP. All Roy Kroc had to know was how to teach people to teach other people how to run a McDonald's restaurant. A business that achieves "product-market fit" has a very specific and path-dependent situation. Sometimes you find this "one weird trick" that lets you make money hand-over-fist for a while and you want most of all to keep that a secret. Other times the knowledge is so specific (how do you grow the most rice you possibly can in this valley?) that it's not of interest to outsiders. "Expert networks" are notoriously promiscuous so firms have a lot of fear that they'll bring in an expert who walks out with more valuable information (e.g. "one weird trick") than the they can bring into it. My favorite kind of expert is this kind of guy [VIDEO] who grew continuously through a 40+ year career and went from being in the dark about noise in circuit boards to an inspiring vision of how electrical energy flows not in the wires but through the space between the wires that makes everything I thought mysterious about antennas seem obvious.

It's easy to listen to, and I'd take him being on any kind of program as an endorsement that it'll be high quality content. The most important talk for beginners getting into high-speed is probably this one: [VIDEO] because without proper grounding, interference and EMI is going to destroy your HF signals (for example CPU to RAM bus).

comments.text_zh: 诚然，我最终做的是一块用微控制器而不是微处理器的板子，因为这样我还能通过 SPI 和调制解调器对接。不过，这个 YouTube 频道非常值得跟着从头做一遍：[LINK] 里面有一些高速相关的内容，涉及 DDR 内存、FPGA 的千兆以太网和 USB3，所以我很确定你可以用同样的思路做一块带微处理器的板子。接地、EMI、阻抗控制和长度匹配都讲得很清楚。我记得他网站上还有更进阶的课程。另外，这个视频让我恍然大悟：[VIDEO]

comments.author: dragontamer
comments.why_zh: 关于 PCB 接地和 PDN 设计的长演讲。
comments.quote_zh: 我觉得你会从这个演讲里受益。
comments.text_zh: 专业人士用的是带物理建模／FEA 的 PCB 设计软件，能估算出电路板所有重要参数（包括走线长度有多重要……还有板级电容、电阻，以及电路板本身的谐振频率等等等等）。相比之下，我们业余爱好者只能靠「经验法则」，因为我们没人愿意花 4000 美元以上去买能替我们跑这些计算的专业 PCB 软件。而且我们把设计做得很保守，因为 PCB 布局问题太难调试了……我们业余爱好者对这些问题是功能性失明的（比如走线电感、走线电容或其他问题）。我觉得花不少时间研究 PDN／接地等等是非常值得的。[VIDEO] 一个 2 个多小时的演讲，专门讲 PCB 里良好「接地」设计的问题，但它确实和电容、走线长度这类问题有关。我觉得你会从这个演讲里受益。「正确」的思维方式极其复杂，远比大学里教的复杂。但多亏了那些老经验法则，你已经有了所有基本概念。你只需要再往前走一步，看看问题都在哪儿。-------- 而且你会看到，板子同一面上的走线是小菜一碟。真正坑你的是过孔之类的东西。
comments.text: The professionals use PCB-design software with physical modeling / FEA to calculate estimates to all of the important parameters of the circuit board (including how much trace lengths matter... but also board-capacitance, resistances, and resonance frequencies of the board itself, etc. etc.) In contrast, we hobbyists deal with "rules of thumb", because none of us will spend $4000+ on professional PCB software that run these calculations for us. And furthermore, we aim very conservative because its very difficult to debug a PCB layout issue... as we hobbyists are functionally blind to all of these issues (ex: trace inductance, trace capacitance, or other issues). I think spending a good bit of time on PDN / grounding / etc. etc. study is very worth your while. [VIDEO] 2+ hour talk on just the issue of good "grounding" design in PCBs, but it does relate to this issue of capacitors, trace-lengths and the like. I feel like you'd benefit from this talk. The "correct" way of thinking is exceptionally complex, far more complex than what is taught in colleges. But you have all the basic ideas thanks to the old rules of thumb. You just need to take the next step to see what the problems are. -------- And as you'll see, traces on the same side of a board are cake. Its things like vias that actually wreck you.

comments.text: This is advanced level PCB design. You need to know proper grounding and differential pairs and length matching to accomplish what is listed in this article. These are very difficult topics, but this 2 hour video should give you an idea of what's going on here: [VIDEO] -------- If this is too much for you, then instead stick to microcontrollers and other sub-100Mhz or sub-20Mhz projects. But 500MHz and above that requires length matching with controlled impedances is waaaayyyyy outside the scope for a beginner designer. --------- Beginner design is easier at 20MHz or so. The faster your signals, the more susceptible to noise they are. Those 500MHz+ Linux MPUs may fail to boot or fail spuriously if you make grounding / noise / EMC errors. And it's pretty difficult to explain to a beginner what is going on physically. The PCB board itself needs to be seen as parasitic capacitors, inductors and resistors (especially around Vias, between layers and other elements). But these 500Mhz or so processors here in this blogpost are still easier than Ghz+ chips. ------ The example I always like to point out: 2.4GHz wavelength is just a couple of cm long. comments.author: nyrikki
comments.story_title: Oliver Heaviside and the theory of transmission lines (2021)
comments.why_zh: 深入讲解介质中的场，把走线看作波导。
comments.quote_zh: Rick Hartley 的这场长篇演讲能帮你更上一层楼。
comments.text_zh: 那个视频里关于水波式的解释很好用，是一个非常有用的视角。如果你想更深入地理解，尤其是场如何在介质中传播、导线和走线只不过是波导这一点，Rick Hartley 的这场长篇演讲能帮你更上一层楼。[VIDEO] 在我看来，到了音频频率以上，行为会发生剧烈变化，水波这个比喻就开始不灵了。前几天我在看我兄弟那张来自 Cray 1a 的内存卡，那个视频突然就浮现在我脑海里。他们的时序走线蜿蜒穿过好几个扁平封装芯片的引脚。难怪即便模块之间全部使用差分双绞线，他们也必须从奇偶校验转向汉明码。
comments.text: That video is good for the water like wave explanation that is a very useful lens. If you want a more in-depth explanation, particularly how the field is in the dielectric and the wires/traces are simply the wave guide, this long presentation by Rick Hartley will help move to the next level. [VIDEO] The dramatic shift in behavior above the audio frequency range is where the water wave lens starts to fall down IMHO. I was looking at my brothers memory card from a Cray 1a the other day and that video popped in my head. They had the timing traces snaking through several flat-pack chips legs. No wonder they had to move from parity to Hamming code even with exclusively using differential twisted pairs between modules.

comments.author: aaronmdjones
comments.story_title: The magic of DC-DC voltage conversion (2023)
comments.why_zh: 关于信号参考平面和 EMI 的进一步材料。
comments.quote_zh: 关于这个主题的一些有趣材料
comments.text_zh: > 那把电源／地放在外层、把信号放在中间不是更好吗？信号绝不能跨过它所参考的平面（通常是 0V 或「ground」）上的断口或缝隙。这会造成严重的 EMI 问题。你的方案会让第 2 层的信号跨过第 1 层地平面上的缝隙（该缝隙是由电源走线造成的）。关于这个主题的一些有趣材料：[LINK] [LINK] [VIDEO] [LINK]
comments.text: > so wouldn't it be better to put power/ground on the outer layers and keep signals in the middle? Signals must never cross a break or split in the plane they're referencing (usually 0V or ""ground""). This creates huge EMI problems. Your proposal would have signals on layer 2 crossing a split in the ground plane on layer 1 (that split caused by power traces). Some interesting material on the subject: [LINK] [LINK] [VIDEO] [LINK]
